turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning, Mr Bell. I'm Jess. I'll just grab your observations before Dr Rahman calls you. Could you pop your arm out?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Good morning. Yes, of course. This one is quite alright.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Ta. Blood pressure is one thirty-eight over eighty-two, pulse seventy-six, temperature thirty-six point seven, and oxygen saturation ninety-eight percent.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you. We were a little late, the traffic on Parramatta Road was dreadful.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Yeah, it's always a car park this hour. Doctor won't be long. There's water just there.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Arthur, Sandra, come in. I'm Dr Rahman. Make yourselves comfortable. What's brought you in?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Good morning, Doctor, and thank you for seeing me. I have a pain in my stomach, and I have been sleeping poorly.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm sorry, that sounds miserable. Tell me about the pain in whatever way makes sense to you.

[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): It is a burning pain, just under the breastbone. It is moderate, and it comes chiefly in the evenings. It has been there since Diwali, or after Diwali. I cannot give you a firm date.
[SEG0010] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Sorry to jump in, I'm Sandra, I live in and look after him. He's playing it down. The pain's all day, he's hardly eating, and he's bringing his dinner back up.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Forgive me, I must correct that. I have not been vomiting. I am still eating, only smaller portions. And the burning is in the evenings, not all day.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): I hear you, Arthur. I'll take your own account of what you feel, and I've heard Sandra too. Does anything set the burning off, or settle it?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): A large meal makes it worse, and lying flat makes it worse. Warm milk eases it a little, and I sleep propped on two pillows.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): How have the nights been, then?
[SEG0015] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Two hours, if that. He's pacing the kitchen at three.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): That is more than the truth, I'm afraid. I do sleep, but I wake several times. It began last winter, or the one before. I cannot say which.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): When you wake, what's going on? The burning, or just wakefulness?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Frequently the burning. At other times I am simply awake. My mind is not especially troubled.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever with this? Black or tarry stools? Trouble swallowing?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. No black stools. I swallow perfectly well.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): And your weight, over this time?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, before I forget, the jacaranda out the front is lovely this week. Um, the weight, I have lost a little, though I have not been on the scales.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ha, they are lovely. A little weight down, without a number, that's fine. Are you on any medicines?

[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): I take two Panadol tablets, five hundred milligrams each, about three evenings a week, when the burning is bad. And amlodipine, ten milligrams... well, actually, five milligrams, every morning, for my blood pressure.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Five milligrams of amlodipine, got it. Anything else, Nurofen or ibuprofen from the chemist?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I do not take those. They have never suited my stomach.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fair enough. Any allergies to medicines, foods, anything?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): None at all. No known allergies.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): How about alcohol? Where does that sit for you?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Only socially.
[SEG0031] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Arthur, come on. It's a bottle most nights. I'm the one picking it up from the bottle shop.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, yes. I was too tidy about it. A bottle of wine most nights, perhaps. I apologise for the first answer.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): No apology needed, and no judgement. I'm glad you've told me. That much wine can stir up the stomach, and I'd like to know how your liver is coping. Do you smoke at all?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): I have never smoked. Not even as a young man.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good. And at home it's you and Sandra?
[SEG0036] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Just us. I do the cooking and the shopping, and I stay over. It's a live-in arrangement.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. It has suited me very well.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mind if I have a feel of your tummy? Hop up on the couch when you're ready.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Certainly. Shall I lie flat?

[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, knees a bit bent if that's easier. Your abdomen is soft, tender just under the breastbone where I'm pressing, with no guarding. I can't feel any lumps, and bowel sounds are present.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, that pressure is the place. It is not unbearable.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Putting this together, it may be gastritis, or it may be reflux. I can't tell those apart today. The evening meals and the wine could both be feeding it.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): I see. I had wondered if it was simply indigestion.
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): It might sit in that family, yes. I'd like to start pantoprazole, forty milligrams, one tablet by mouth, every morning, half an hour before breakfast, for the burning.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): I shall take it exactly so. Do I get it from the chemist?
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, I'll write the script. And I'll order liver blood tests today, because of the wine, to see how the liver is travelling. Jess can take the blood after we're done.
[SEG0047] person_1 (NURSE): I'll do the bloods straight after, no worries. Tubes are ready out the back.

[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): In the meantime, smaller evening meals, ease back on the wine if you can manage it, and stay propped up after dinner rather than lying flat. If you vomit blood, or the pain becomes severe and sudden, don't wait on me, go to emergency.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): I understand. I will be careful, and I will go to emergency if that happens.
[SEG0050] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I'll keep an eye, and I'll cut the wine down in the shopping.
[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): That would help. Come back in a fortnight and we'll go through the blood results. You're both welcome.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): A fortnight. Thank you, Doctor. You have been very clear, and very kind.
[SEG0053] person_4 (CAREGIVER): We'll book it on the way out. Thanks.
